metadata.title: SOGC Statement on Rh and Alloimmunization
metadata.summary: This statement examines evidence on Rh alloimmunization after abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation and explains the SOGC position that avoiding routine RhIg may be considered through individualized decision-making. It also discusses access, confidentiality and RhIg supply, and compares recommendations from health professional organizations.

target_population: Rh-negative unsensitized patients undergoing abortion or experiencing pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation
pregnant individuals requiring Rh D blood typing or assessment for Rho(D) immune globulin
therapeutic_areas: blood group typing and antibody screening

therapies_index.name: RhIg
therapies_index.mechanism: Given to prevent Rh D sensitisation.
approved_indications: The SOGC recommends prophylaxis for pregnant individuals with other weak D variants or partial D; it does not recommend prophylaxis for weak D types 1, 2, and 3.
NICE recommends prophylaxis after 10+0 weeks' gestation for rhesus D negative women having an abortion and recommends considering it for surgical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.
NICE recommends prophylaxis for rhesusnegative women undergoing a surgical procedure to manage an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage.
The National Abortion Federation states that it must be offered to Rh negative patients over 12 weeks from the last menstrual period.

The Society for Maternal fetal Medicine recommends it for unsensitized, RhDnegative individuals with spontaneous or induced abortion at <12 weeks of gestation when testing and administration are feasible and do not impede abortion care.
WHO states that usual anti-D care applies at gestational ages ≥ 12 weeks; it recommends against administration for medical or surgical abortion at < 12 weeks.
therapies_index.administration: NICE specifies 250 IU (50 micrograms) for rhesusnegative women undergoing a surgical procedure to manage an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage. WHO mentions antenatal prophylaxis at 28 and 34 weeks of gestation in the context of rigorous research.

therapies_index.name: uterine aspiration
approved_indications: The ACOG update identifies it as a way to manage abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 0/7 weeks of gestation.

therapies_index.name: medication abortion
approved_indications: The National Abortion Federation discusses it as a method of abortion below 12 weeks from the last menstrual period.

therapies_index.name: surgical abortion
approved_indications: The cited guidance discusses it as an abortion method, including at gestational ages up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation and at less than 12 weeks.

therapies_index.name: medication management of EPL
approved_indications: The Society of Family Planning discusses this approach for EPL before 12 weeks of gestation.

therapies_index.name: medical management for an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage
approved_indications: NICE identifies medical management as an approach for ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage.

therapies_index.name: surgical procedure to manage an ectopic pregnancy or a miscarriage
approved_indications: NICE identifies surgical management as an approach for ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage.

prophylaxis.recommendation: The SOGC statement allows clinicians to consider omitting RhIg in early pregnancy. It does not prohibit administration and supports shared decisions that take account of individual circumstances, risk aversion and future pregnancy plans.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients with abortion or pregnancy loss in early pregnancy

prophylaxis.recommendation: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada recommends against prophylaxis for weak D types 1, 2, and 3, which it states carry no alloimmunization risk. It recommends prophylaxis for other weak D variants or partial D because of potential alloimmunization risk.
prophylaxis.target_population: Pregnant individuals with weak D types 1, 2, and 3, other weak D variants, or partial D

prophylaxis.recommendation: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists does not routinely indicate Rh testing or RhIg administration, but permits individual consideration through shared discussion of potential benefits and risks.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients at less than 12 0/7 weeks of gestation undergoing abortion or experiencing pregnancy loss, whether spontaneous or managed with uterine aspiration or medication

prophylaxis.recommendation: The Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommends administration for abortion in Rh D negative women; individualized care may also be considered according to the person's risk–benefit profile.
prophylaxis.target_population: Rh D negative women having an abortion at 10 weeks or more

prophylaxis.recommendation: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guideline on abortion care advises offering prophylaxis. Providers should have it available when the abortion takes place and ensure that its supply, or rhesus status testing, does not delay care.
prophylaxis.target_population: Rhesus D negative women having an abortion after 10+0 weeks' gestation

prophylaxis.recommendation: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guideline on abortion care advises against offering prophylaxis.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women having a medical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation

prophylaxis.recommendation: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guideline on abortion care advises considering prophylaxis.
prophylaxis.target_population: Rhesus D negative women having a surgical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation

prophylaxis.recommendation: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guideline on ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage advises offering a dose of 250 IU (50 micrograms).
prophylaxis.target_population: All rhesus-negative women undergoing a surgical procedure to manage an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage

prophylaxis.recommendation: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guideline on ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage advises against offering prophylaxis.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women managed solely with medication for ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage, or with threatened miscarriage, complete miscarriage, or pregnancy of unknown location

prophylaxis.recommendation: The World Health Organization recommends against administration for either medical or surgical abortion.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients having an abortion at < 12 weeks

prophylaxis.recommendation: The World Health Organization specifies that standard care for administration applies.
The World Health Organization states that it recommends antenatal prophylaxis at 28 and 34 weeks of gestation only in the context of rigorous research.
The National Abortion Federation requires that prophylaxis be offered to Rh negative patients.
prophylaxis.target_population: Rh negative patients over 12 weeks from the last menstrual period (LMP)

prophylaxis.recommendation: The National Abortion Federation permits patients and providers to omit prophylaxis for either medication abortion or aspiration procedures.
prophylaxis.target_population: Rh negative patients below 12 weeks from the last menstrual period

prophylaxis.recommendation: The Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine recommends administration alongside RhD testing when both are logistically and financially feasible and do not impede access to abortion care.
prophylaxis.target_population: Unsensitized, RhDnegative individuals with spontaneous or induced abortion at <12 weeks of gestation in care settings meeting those conditions

prophylaxis.recommendation: The Society of Family Planning suggests against administration. Although it is not recommended, administration may be considered at the patient's request through shared decision-making that addresses future fertility wishes and the available evidence.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients receiving medication management of EPL before 12 weeks of gestation

prophylaxis.recommendation: The Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists states that prophylaxis is not required for surgical abortion.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients having a surgical abortion at less than 12 weeks of pregnancy

conditions.name: Rh alloimmunization
conditions.description: Sensitization can occur when an Rh-negative pregnant individual is exposed to fetal Rh D antigen and develops antibodies. It may affect a subsequent pregnancy.
conditions.epidemiology: Recent studies cited in the statement consistently associate abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation with a very low risk of Rh alloimmunization. A 2021 systematic review found no significantly higher alloimmunization rates when RhIg was withheld in the first trimester.

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: The cited SOGC guideline recommends testing at the first prenatal visit after 8 weeks gestation and advises against routine testing before 8 weeks gestation.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A discrepant, weak, or inconclusive Rh D result warrants further investigation with RHD genotyping under the cited SOGC guideline.

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: The cited SOGC guideline recommends screening at the first prenatal visit after 8 weeks gestation and advises against routine screening before 8 weeks gestation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Clarify eligibility for Rho(D) immune globulin when Rh D typing is discrepant, weak, or inconclusive.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Prenatal patients with discrepant, weak, or inconclusive Rh D blood typing, according to the cited SOGC guideline.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Weak D types 1, 2, and 3 are described as carrying no alloimmunization risk; other weak D variants and partial D are described as carrying potential risk.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: The cited SOGC guideline describes these types as carrying no risk of alloimmunization.
The cited SOGC guideline describes a potential risk of alloimmunization.
The cited SOGC guideline describes a potential risk of alloimmunization.

long_term_effects: Maternal antibodies resulting from Rh D sensitisation may cause fetal anaemia in a subsequent pregnancy.

conditions.name: abortion
conditions.description: The statement addresses abortion at early gestational ages, including medication and aspiration or surgical procedures, in relation to Rh testing and prophylaxis.
conditions.epidemiology: Recent studies cited in the statement associate abortion at less than 12 weeks of gestation with a very low risk of Rh alloimmunization.

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: The cited Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists guideline advises clinical judgement about selective testing in women at increased haemorrhage risk, including anaemia or advanced gestation.

document_sections.heading: SOGC Statement on Rh and Alloimmunization
document_sections.content: Before 2021, organizations including the SOGC and the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) advised routine RhIg after abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation for all unsensitized Rh-negative patients. That advice rested on little or very low-quality evidence: the anticipated prevention of Rh alloimmunization was considered more important than the negligible medical risks and economic costs of immunization. More recent studies consistently indicate a very low risk of Rh alloimmunization after abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks. Earlier support for prophylaxis was largely retrospective, used outdated methods to quantify fetal-maternal hemorrhage (FMH), usually measured FMH rather than subsequent alloimmunization, and did not establish a fetal-blood-transfer threshold requiring prophylaxis. Studies initially favoring early RhIg were performed in the 1970s with abortion techniques that may have increased FMH risk. A 2021 systematic review found no significantly higher alloimmunization rates when RhIg was withheld in the first trimester. Subsequently, guidance from the SOGC, ACOG, the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG), the World Health Organization (WHO), the Society for Family Planning, and several European professional bodies ceased to recommend routine RhIg for abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks. Current guidance generally reserves RhIg for later gestations, usually beyond 10 to 12 weeks, or calls for individualized decisions based on risk. Older guidance is more likely to endorse routine use; guidance issued in the last five years increasingly favors a more selective, patient-centered approach. In Canada, hospital-based RhIg administration can increase emergency department visits and clinic workload despite an unconfirmed benefit in early pregnancy; avoiding unnecessary use could reduce waits and system strain. Where a rural area has only one ABO and Rh testing facility, testing can unintentionally reveal an early abortion or miscarriage. The SOGC does not prohibit RhIg: it encourages shared decisions that account for individual circumstances, risk aversion, and plans for future pregnancy. An international RhIg shortage limits access in some low- and middle-income countries even for high-risk indications, including administration at 28 weeks and after delivery; reducing use for unproven indications could preserve supply for patients with demonstrated benefit. The updated SOGC position accords with policies of the WHO, RCOG, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), the Society for Family Planning, Sweden, France, and the Netherlands. The Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM) is identified as the only major organization that still recommends RhIg for every early pregnancy loss and abortion, a position the statement says does not reflect broader international obstetric guidance. In light of these considerations, the SOGC considers allowing clinicians to contemplate omitting RhIg in early pregnancy a reasonable, evidence-based position. It acknowledges that research continues to develop and intends to monitor new findings.

document_sections.heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks
document_sections.content: The table compares professional organizations’ guidance concerning RhIG, Rh testing, and related care for early pregnancy loss and abortion. It presents the organizations and guideline titles alongside their recommendations, the stated recommendation strength or type of evidence, and references. The guidance varies by gestational age, clinical circumstance, and approach to shared decision-making.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant individuals before 8 weeks gestation.
decision_rules: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada advises against routine blood group typing and antibody screening before 8 weeks gestation.

not_recommended.name: Routine blood group typing and antibody screening
not_recommended.reason: Not recommended before 8 weeks gestation; the cited recommendation is graded GRADE: conditional, low.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: All pregnant individuals attending their first prenatal visit after 8 weeks gestation.
decision_rules: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada recommends blood group typing and antibody screening at this visit.

recommended_regimens.name: Blood group typing and antibody screening
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform both tests at the first prenatal visit after 8 weeks gestation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Prenatal patients whose Rh D blood typing is discrepant, weak, or inconclusive.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: Discrepant, weak, or inconclusive Rh D blood typing.
decision_rules: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada recommends RHD genotyping to establish whether Rho(D) immune globulin is indicated.
Do not give Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis for Weak D types 1, 2, and 3; give it for other weak D variants or partial D.

recommended_regimens.name: RHD genotyping
recommended_regimens.summary: Investigate an uncertain Rh D typing result to guide eligibility for Rho(D) immune globulin.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited guideline states that Weak D types 1, 2, and 3 carry no alloimmunization risk, whereas other weak D variants and partial D may carry a risk.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant individuals with Weak D types 1, 2, and 3.
decision_rules: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada advises against Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis for these genotypes.

not_recommended.name: Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis
not_recommended.reason: The cited guideline states that Weak D types 1, 2, and 3 carry no risk of alloimmunization.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Pregnant individuals with other weak D variants or partial D.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: Other weak D variants, or partial D
decision_rules: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada recommends Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis because alloimmunization is possible.

recommended_regimens.name: Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide prophylaxis for other weak D variants or partial D.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients having an abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation.
decision_rules: The SOGC statement allows consideration of forgoing RhIg in early pregnancy rather than requiring its omission.
Use shared decision-making when considering RhIg, including the patient's risk aversion and plans for future pregnancies.

alternative_regimens.name: RhIg
alternative_regimens.summary: Administration remains an option after an individualized discussion.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider the patient's circumstances, risk preferences, and future pregnancy plans.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The statement describes the reported risk of Rh alloimmunization after abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation as very low. It also cites access, confidentiality, and global RhIg supply as considerations.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients at less than 12 0/7 weeks of gestation having an abortion managed with uterine aspiration or medication, or experiencing spontaneous pregnancy loss or pregnancy loss managed with uterine aspiration or medication.
decision_rules: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists states that routine Rh testing and RhIg administration are not indicated, but either may be considered individually through shared decision-making about possible benefits and risks.

alternative_regimens.name: Rh testing and RhIg administration
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider these measures for an individual patient despite their absence from routine care.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: An individualized shared decision-making discussion supports their use.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited update attributes a very low likelihood of Rh alloimmunization after abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation to recent studies.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Individuals having a medical or surgical abortion up to 10 weeks pregnant.
decision_rules: The Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists does not require routine blood group testing for Rh D status before abortion up to 10 weeks.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited guideline describes the certainty of evidence as No direct evidence.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women at increased risk of haemorrhage before abortion, including those with anaemia or advanced gestation.
decision_rules: The Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists calls for clinical judgement about selective pre-abortion testing of haemoglobin and blood group.

alternative_regimens.name: Selective testing of haemoglobin and blood group
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider these tests before abortion according to clinical judgement.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Increased haemorrhage risk, including but not limited to anaemia or advanced gestation.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited guideline states that the benefits and risks of preprocedure haemoglobin or Rh D testing are unclear.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Rh D negative women having an abortion in pregnancies 10 weeks or more.
decision_rules: The Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommends Anti-D administration for this group.
Individualised care based on the patient's risk-benefit profile could be considered.

recommended_regimens.name: Anti-D
recommended_regimens.summary: Administer for abortion in pregnancies 10 weeks or more in Rh D negative women.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited guideline describes prevention of Rh D sensitisation as the purpose of Anti-D.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women who are rhesus D negative and are having an abortion after 10+0 weeks' gestation.
decision_rules: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence recommends offering anti-D prophylaxis.
Rhesus status testing and obtaining anti-D must not delay abortion care, and prophylaxis should be available when the abortion takes place.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women having a medical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.
decision_rules: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises against offering anti-D prophylaxis in this setting.

not_recommended.name: anti-D prophylaxis
not_recommended.reason: The cited guideline directs providers not to offer it for medical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited guideline reports that its systematic review identified no studies comparing Anti-D prophylaxis with no Anti-D prophylaxis among women having an abortion prior to 13 completed weeks.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women who are rhesus D negative and are having a surgical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.
decision_rules: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises considering anti-D prophylaxis rather than routinely requiring it.
Testing and prophylaxis supply should not delay abortion; anti-D should be available at the time of the procedure.

alternative_regimens.name: anti-D prophylaxis
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider prophylaxis for surgical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The patient is rhesus D negative and is having a surgical abortion.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: All rhesusnegative women undergoing a surgical procedure to manage an ectopic pregnancy or a miscarriage.
decision_rules: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence recommends anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis for surgical management.

recommended_regimens.name: anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis
recommended_regimens.summary: Give 250 IU (50 micrograms) when a surgical procedure is used to manage an ectopic pregnancy or a miscarriage.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women receiving solely medical management for an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage, or women with a threatened miscarriage, complete miscarriage, or pregnancy of unknown location.
decision_rules: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises against offering anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis in each of these circumstances.

not_recommended.name: anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis
not_recommended.reason: The cited guideline directs providers not to offer it with solely medical management of an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage, threatened miscarriage, complete miscarriage, or pregnancy of unknown location.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Individuals having a medical or surgical abortion at < 12 weeks.
decision_rules: The World Health Organization recommends against anti-D immunoglobulin administration for either abortion method at < 12 weeks.

not_recommended.name: anti-D immunoglobulin administration
not_recommended.reason: The cited expert panel judged that the evidence overall did not favour routine administration after considering resource requirements, cost-effectiveness, feasibility, and very low certainty of evidence on effectiveness.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The World Health Organization's cited review found few studies of Rh isoimmunization in unsensitized Rh-negative individuals seeking abortion before 12 weeks of gestation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Individuals at gestational ages ≥ 12 weeks.
decision_rules: The World Health Organization states that usual care for anti-D administration applies at gestational ages ≥ 12 weeks.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People over 12 weeks from the last menstrual period (LMP) whose Rh status is unknown; patients over 12 weeks who are Rh negative.
decision_rules: The National Abortion Federation requires that Rh status testing be offered when status is unknown and that anti-D immune globulin be offered to patients who are Rh negative.

recommended_regimens.name: Rh status testing
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer testing to everyone with unknown Rh status over 12 weeks from LMP.

recommended_regimens.name: anti-D immune globulin
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer prophylaxis to patients over 12 weeks who are Rh negative.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients below 12 weeks from the last menstrual period having a medication abortion or aspiration procedure.
decision_rules: The National Abortion Federation permits patients and providers to forgo Rh testing and anti-D immune globulin below 12 weeks from LMP.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited policy states that there is no evidence that anti-D immunoglobulin in early pregnancy prevents alloimmunization and poor outcomes in a later pregnancy. It also describes additional testing and treatment as burdensome.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Unsensitized, RhDnegative individuals having a spontaneous or induced abortion at <12 weeks of gestation in care settings where testing and administration are logistically and financially feasible and do not hinder access to abortion care.
decision_rules: The Society for Maternal fetal Medicine recommends both RhD testing and RhIg administration when the stated feasibility and access conditions are met.

recommended_regimens.name: RhD testing and RhIg administration
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide both measures for spontaneous or induced abortion at <12 weeks of gestation when they are feasible and do not impede care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients undergoing medication management of EPL before 12 weeks of gestation.
decision_rules: The Society of Family Planning suggests against Rh testing and Rh-immunoglobulin administration.
At the patient's request, either measure may nevertheless be considered through shared decision-making that addresses future fertility desires and existing data.

alternative_regimens.name: Rh testing and Rh-immunoglobulin administration
alternative_regimens.summary: Although not recommended routinely, these measures may be considered at the patient's request.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Shared decision-making that includes the patient's future fertility desires.

not_recommended.name: Routine Rh testing and Rh-immunoglobulin administration
not_recommended.reason: The cited Society of Family Planning recommendation suggests against these measures before 12 weeks of gestation for medication management of EPL; Grade 2B.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Individuals seeking an abortion, including those having a surgical abortion at less than 12 weeks pregnant.
decision_rules: The Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists does not require routine blood tests during pre-abortion assessment.
Rhesus blood status determination may be considered when pregnancy duration exceeds 12 weeks and anti-D is available.
Haemoglobin concentration or other blood tests are unnecessary unless there is a sound clinical indication, such as symptomatic anaemia.

alternative_regimens.name: Rhesus blood status determination
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider determining blood status as part of pre-abortion assessment.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Pregnancy duration is over 12 weeks and anti-D is available.

alternative_regimens.name: Measurement of haemoglobin concentration or other blood tests
alternative_regimens.summary: Use blood tests when clinically indicated rather than as routine assessment.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: A clinical indication exists, such as symptomatic anaemia.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists consensus states that Anti-D prophylaxis is not required for surgical abortion at less than 12 weeks pregnant. It attributes this position to studies indicating that fetal red blood cell exposure remains below the calculated threshold for maternal Rh D sensitization.

rows: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada (2024)
Guideline No. 448: Prevention of Rh D Alloimmunization

Routine blood group typing and antibody screening are not recommended before 8 weeks gestation. Blood group typing and antibody screening are recommended for all pregnant individuals at their first prenatal visit after 8 weeks gestation. Discrepant, weak, or inconclusive Rh D typing warrants RHD genotyping to establish eligibility for Rho(D) immune globulin. Prophylaxis is not recommended for weak D types 1, 2, and 3, which carry no alloimmunization risk; it is recommended for other weak D variants or partial D because they carry potential risk.
GRADE: conditional, low; Good Practice Point; GRADE: strong, moderate
Fung-Kee-Fung K, Wong K, Walsh J, et al.; J Obstet Gynaecol Can. 2024;46:102449. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov /pubmed/38553007
The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (2024)
ACOG Clinical Practice Update: Rh D Immune Globulin Administration After Abortion or Pregnancy Loss at Less Than 12 Weeks of Gestation

For abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 0/7 weeks of gestation, whether spontaneous or managed with medication or uterine aspiration, Rh testing and RhIg are not routinely indicated. They may nevertheless be considered individually through shared discussion of potential benefits and risks.
Recent studies suggest a very low likelihood of Rh alloimmunization after abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation.

ACOG Clinical Practice Update: Rh D Immune Globulin Administration After Abortion or Pregnancy Loss at Less Than 12 Weeks of Gestation; Obstet Gynecol. 2024 Dec 1;144(6):e140e143. doi: 10.1097/AOG.000000000000 5733. Epub 2024 Sep 10. PMID: 39255498.
Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (2023)
Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care

Routine Rh D blood group testing is not required before medical or surgical abortion up to 10 weeks pregnant. Clinical judgement should guide selective haemoglobin and blood group testing before abortion when haemorrhage risk is increased, including with anaemia or advanced gestation. Anti-D is recommended for Rh D negative women undergoing abortion in pregnancies 10 weeks or more; individualised care may be considered according to the person’s risk-benefit profile.

Evidence source: systematic review, two additional studies, and annual reports from the Serious Hazards of Transfusion (SHOT) database. Certainty of evidence: No direct evidence. Benefits and risks of preprocedure haemoglobin or Rh D testing are unclear. Exposure of Rh D negative women to fetal Rh D antigen may lead to sensitisation, antibodies against Rh-positive red blood cells (RBCs), and fetal anaemia in a later pregnancy; Anti-D is given to prevent sensitisation.
Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidencebased guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (2023). RANZCOG, Melbourne, Australia.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2019)
Abortion care: NICE guideline [NG140]

Offer anti-D after 10+0 weeks' gestation to rhesus D negative women having an abortion. Do not offer it for medical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation. Consider it for rhesus D negative women having surgical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation. Providers should prevent rhesus testing or anti-D supply from delaying abortion and make anti-D available when the abortion takes place.
A systematic review for this guideline identified no studies comparing Anti-D prophylaxis with no prophylaxis for abortion before 13 completed weeks.
Abortion care: Nice guideline (ng140). London, UK: Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists; 2019.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2023)
Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management NICE guideline [NG126]

Offer anti-D immunoglobulin at 250 IU (50 micrograms) to every rhesus-negative woman undergoing a surgical procedure for ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage. Do not offer it for exclusively medical management of ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage, threatened miscarriage, complete miscarriage, or pregnancy of unknown location.
Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management. London: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE); 2023 Aug 23. PMID: 31393678.
World Health Organization (2022)
Recommend against anti-D immunoglobulin for medical or surgical abortion at < 12 weeks. Standard care for anti-D applies at ≥ 12 weeks.

A systematic review found few studies of Rh isoimmunization among unsensitized Rh-negative individuals seeking abortion before 12 weeks: only two studies, from Israel and the USA and both published in 1972, met its criteria. Antibody formation after the initial pregnancy was less frequent with anti-D than without it, and no intervention harms were noted, so effectiveness evidence might favour treatment. Nevertheless, its certainty was very low; after considering resources, cost-effectiveness, and feasibility, the expert panel judged that the evidence overall did not favour treatment at < 12 weeks rather than the < 9 weeks threshold in 2012 guidance. Its reasons included that fetal blood exposure early in pregnancy does not necessarily produce alloimmunization; application of an experimental study would theoretically imply zero chance of antibody formation after exposure to fetal Rh-antigen; a comparison between two countries supported not treating Rhnegative women with spontaneous abortion under 10 weeks of gestation; and WHO recommends antenatal anti-D for nonsensitized Rh-negative pregnant women at 28 and 34 weeks of gestation only within rigorous research.
WHO. Abortion care guideline. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2022.
National Abortion Federation (2024)
Clinical policy guidelines for abortion care

Rh status testing must be offered when Rh status is unknown over 12 weeks from the last menstrual period (LMP); anti-D immune globulin must be offered over 12 weeks to Rh-negative patients. Below 12 weeks from LMP, patients and providers may omit Rh testing and anti-D immune globulin for Rh-negative patients undergoing medication abortion or aspiration. The policy notes that Rh alloimmunization may harm a later pregnancy, that evidence does not establish prevention of alloimmunization or poor later-pregnancy outcomes by early anti-D, and that anti-D is recommended later in pregnancy.

Epidemiologic and clinical evidence indicates negligible maternal-fetal haemorrhage risk from early abortion. Benefit from Rh testing and anti-D in early abortion has not been shown, while additional testing and treatment burden patients and providers; foregoing both before 12 weeks LMP is therefore considered reasonable.
National abortion federation. Clinical policy guidelines for abortion care. 2024.
Society for Maternal fetal Medicine (2024)
Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine Statement: RhD immune globulin after spontaneous 2 or induced abortion less than 12 weeks of gestation

Recommend RhD testing and RhIg for unsensitized, RhDnegative individuals with spontaneous or induced abortion at <12 weeks of gestation where testing and administration are logistically and financially feasible and do not impede abortion access.
None given
Society of Family Planning (2024)

Suggest against Rh testing and Rh-immunoglobulin before 12 weeks of gestation for medication management of EPL. Although not recommended, testing and administration may be considered at the patient’s request through shared decision-making that addresses future fertility wishes and existing evidence.
Grade 2B

Tarleton JL, Benson LS, Moayedi G, Trevino J; with assistance from Leah Coplon, Anitra Beasley, and Elise Boos on behalf of the Society of Family Planning Clinical Affairs Committee. Society of Family Planning Clinical Recommendation: Medication management for early pregnancy loss. Contraception. 2024 Dec 20:110805. doi: 10.1016/j.contraception.2024 .110805. Epub ahead of print. PMID: 39710335.
Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists (2022)
Best Practice in Abortion Care

Routine blood tests are not required before abortion. Rhesus status assessment may be considered when pregnancy exceeds 12 weeks and anti-D is available. Haemoglobin measurement or other blood tests are unnecessary unless clinically indicated, for example by symptomatic anaemia.

Consensus held that Anti-D prophylaxis is unnecessary for surgical abortion before 12 weeks, based on studies finding fetal red blood cell exposure below the calculated threshold for maternal Rh D sensitization.
Best practice in abortion care. London, UK: The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists; 2022.

artifacts.description: The appendix presents one comparison across successive pages. The SOGC row lists GRADE: conditional, low; Good Practice Point; and GRADE: strong, moderate in sequence for its recommendations.
artifacts.summary: This table compares organizational positions on Rh testing and anti-D or RhIg around early abortion and pregnancy loss, alongside their stated evidence and references.
artifacts.clinical_relevance: It distinguishes recommendations to omit routine prophylaxis from circumstances in which testing or prophylaxis is offered, recommended, or considered, including differing gestational thresholds and approaches to shared decision-making.

recommendations.statement: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada advises against routine blood group typing and antibody screening before 8 weeks gestation.
recommendations.context: Pregnant individuals.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada recommends blood group typing and antibody screening at the first prenatal visit after 8 weeks gestation.
recommendations.context: All pregnant individuals.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada recommends RHD genotyping when Rh D blood typing is discrepant, weak, or inconclusive, to establish whether Rho(D) immune globulin is indicated.
recommendations.context: Prenatal patients with discrepant, weak, or inconclusive Rh D blood typing.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada advises against Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis for individuals with Weak D types 1, 2, and 3.
recommendations.context: Individuals with Weak D types 1, 2, and 3.
recommendations.rationale: These types carry no risk of alloimmunization.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada recommends Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis for individuals with other weak D variants or partial D.
recommendations.context: Individuals with weak D variants other than Weak D types 1, 2, and 3, or with partial D.
recommendations.rationale: These variants carry a potential risk of alloimmunization.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists does not routinely indicate Rh testing or RhIg administration, but permits individual consideration through shared decision-making about potential benefits and risks.
recommendations.context: Patients at less than 12 0/7 weeks of gestation undergoing abortion or experiencing pregnancy loss, whether spontaneous or managed with uterine aspiration or medication.
recommendations.rationale: Recent studies suggest a very low likelihood of Rh alloimmunization after abortion or pregnancy loss at less than 12 weeks of gestation.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists does not require routine Rh D blood group testing before medical or surgical abortion up to 10 weeks pregnant.
recommendations.context: Medical or surgical abortion up to 10 weeks pregnant.
recommendations.rationale: The stated supporting evidence includes a systematic review, two studies, and reports from the Serious Hazards of Transfusion (SHOT) database.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists advises using clinical judgement about selective haemoglobin and blood group testing before abortion when haemorrhage risk is increased.
recommendations.context: Women at increased risk of haemorrhage, including those with anaemia or advanced gestation.
recommendations.rationale: The benefits and risks of preprocedure haemoglobin or Rh D testing are unclear.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommends Anti-D administration for Rh D negative women having an abortion at 10 weeks or more.
recommendations.context: Rh D negative women having an abortion in pregnancies 10 weeks or more.
recommendations.rationale: Exposure to fetal blood cells can sensitise Rh D negative women and may cause fetal anaemia in a subsequent pregnancy.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Royal Australia and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists permits consideration of individualised care according to the patient's risk-benefit profile.
recommendations.context: Rh D negative women having an abortion in pregnancies 10 weeks or more.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence recommends offering anti-D prophylaxis to rhesus D negative women having an abortion after 10+0 weeks' gestation.
recommendations.context: Abortion after 10+0 weeks' gestation.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises against offering anti-D prophylaxis for medical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.
recommendations.context: Medical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.
recommendations.rationale: A systematic review found no studies comparing Anti-D prophylaxis with no Anti-D prophylaxis for abortion before 13 completed weeks.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises considering anti-D prophylaxis for rhesus D negative women having a surgical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.
recommendations.context: Surgical abortion up to and including 10+0 weeks' gestation.
recommendations.rationale: A systematic review found no studies comparing Anti-D prophylaxis with no Anti-D prophylaxis for abortion before 13 completed weeks.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence says providers should prevent rhesus status testing or anti-D prophylaxis supply from delaying abortion and should make anti-D prophylaxis available when the abortion takes place.
recommendations.context: Abortion care providers.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence recommends offering anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis at 250 IU (50 micrograms) to rhesusnegative women undergoing a surgical procedure for an ectopic pregnancy or a miscarriage.
recommendations.context: Surgical management of an ectopic pregnancy or a miscarriage.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises against anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis when an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage is managed solely with medication.
recommendations.context: Solely medical management.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises against offering anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis for threatened miscarriage.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises against offering anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis for complete miscarriage.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises against offering anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis for a pregnancy of unknown location.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The World Health Organization recommends against anti-D immunoglobulin administration for either medical or surgical abortion at < 12 weeks.
recommendations.context: Medical or surgical abortion at < 12 weeks.
recommendations.evidence_level: very low certainty of the evidence on effectiveness
recommendations.rationale: The expert panel judged that the evidence overall did not favour administration after considering effectiveness alongside resources, cost-effectiveness, and feasibility.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The World Health Organization specifies that standard care for anti-D administration applies at gestational ages ≥ 12 weeks.
recommendations.context: Abortion at gestational ages ≥ 12 weeks.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The World Health Organization recommends antenatal anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis at 28 and 34 weeks of gestation only in the context of rigorous research.
recommendations.context: Nonsensitized Rh-negative pregnant women; prevention of RhD alloimmunization.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Abortion Federation requires offering Rh status testing to all people whose Rh status is unknown and who are over 12 weeks from the last menstrual period (LMP).
recommendations.context: People over 12 weeks from the last menstrual period (LMP) with unknown Rh status.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Abortion Federation requires offering anti-D immune globulin to Rh negative patients who are over 12 weeks from the last menstrual period (LMP).
recommendations.context: Rh negative patients over 12 weeks from the last menstrual period (LMP).
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The National Abortion Federation permits patients and providers to omit Rh testing and anti-D immune globulin below 12 weeks from the last menstrual period, including for medication abortion and aspiration procedures.
recommendations.context: Rh negative patients below 12 weeks from the last menstrual period.
recommendations.rationale: The organization states that benefit from Rh testing and anti-D immune globulin in early abortion has not been demonstrated and that additional testing and treatment burden patients and providers.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Society for Maternal fetal Medicine recommends both RhD testing and RhIg administration after spontaneous or induced abortion at <12 weeks of gestation when these measures are logistically and financially feasible and do not impede abortion access.
recommendations.context: Unsensitized, RhDnegative individuals in care settings meeting the stated feasibility and access conditions.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Society of Family Planning suggests against Rh testing and Rh-immunoglobulin administration before 12 weeks of gestation during medication management of EPL.
recommendations.context: Patients undergoing medication management of EPL before 12 weeks of gestation.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Society of Family Planning permits consideration of Rh testing and Rhimmunoglobulin administration at a patient's request, despite not recommending them, through shared decision-making that considers future fertility wishes and existing data.
recommendations.context: Patients undergoing medication management of EPL before 12 weeks of gestation who request testing or administration.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists states that routine blood tests are unnecessary for pre-abortion assessment.
recommendations.context: Pre-abortion assessment.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists permits consideration of Rhesus blood status determination when pregnancy duration exceeds 12 weeks and anti-D is available.
recommendations.context: Pregnancy duration over 12 weeks when anti-D is available.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists does not require haemoglobin measurement or other blood tests unless a sound clinical indication exists, such as symptomatic anaemia.
recommendations.context: Pre-abortion assessment.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks

recommendations.statement: The Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists considers Anti-D prophylaxis unnecessary for surgical abortion at less than 12 weeks pregnant.
recommendations.context: Surgical abortion at less than 12 weeks pregnant.
recommendations.rationale: The stated consensus draws on studies indicating that fetal red blood cell exposure during surgical abortion under 12 weeks falls below the calculated threshold for maternal Rh D sensitization.
recommendations.source_heading: Appendix 1: Summary of Guidelines from Health Professional Organizations for RhIG for Early Pregnancy Loss and Abortion < 12 weeks
